response.title: which dehumidifiers work in a cold garage or basement
response.answer:
For a cold garage or basement, you need a dehumidifier designed for low temperatures. Many ordinary household dehumidifiers become ineffective or develop ice on their coils when temperatures drop below 60°F (16°C).

The best choice depends on how cold the space gets.

Which type works at which temperature?

Important: A dehumidifier advertised as having automatic defrost isn't necessarily designed to operate near freezing. Check its specified minimum operating temperature.

markup:
For a **cold garage or basement**, you need a dehumidifier designed for low temperatures. Many ordinary household dehumidifiers become ineffective or develop ice on their coils when temperatures drop below 60°F (16°C).

The best choice depends on how cold the space gets.

## Which type works at which temperature?

| Temperature | Best type | What to expect |
|---|---|---|
| 60–80°F (16–27°C) | Standard compressor | Efficient and widely available |
| 41–60°F (5–16°C) | Low-temperature compressor with auto-defrost | Good for most cool basements |
| 33–41°F (1–5°C) | Desiccant or specialized low-temp unit | Better than typical compressor models |
| Below 32°F (0°C) | Specialized desiccant system | Most residential units are unsuitable |

**Important:** A dehumidifier advertised as having *automatic defrost* isn't necessarily designed to operate near freezing. Check its specified minimum operating temperature.
